questions.question: Define Personality and its components. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Defence mechanisms reduce emotional distress without solving the underlying problem.
  • Types of Defence mechanism
  •  Repression – pushing painful thoughts into the unconscious mind.
  •  Denial – refusing to accept reality or facts (common in trauma or illness).
  •  Projection – attributing one’s own unacceptable feelings to others.
  •  Displacement – redirecting emotions to a safer substitute target.
  •  Regression – reverting to earlier developmental behaviors under stress (e.g., childlike behavior).
  •  Rationalization & Sublimation – justifying behavior logically or channeling impulses into socially
  • acceptable activities (healthy mechanism).

questions.question: Explain the utility of Humanistic and Cognitive Approaches in addressing Human behaviour. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the utility of Humanistic and Cognitive Approaches in addressing Human
  • behaviour.
  • Humanistic Approach:
  • o Focuses on individual potential, personal growth, and self-
  • actualization.
  • o Helps in understanding subjective experiences, emotions, and self-
  • concept.
  • o Useful in therapy (e.g., client-centered therapy by Carl Rogers),
  • education, and counseling by promoting self-awareness and positive self-
  • regard.
  • Cognitive Approach:
  • o Emphasizes mental processes such as perception, memory, thinking,
  • and problem-solving.
  • o Useful in understanding irrational thoughts, treating cognitive
  • distortions (as in CBT), and improving learning strategies.
  • o Provides insights into decision-making, attention, and language use.
  • Together, these approaches offer a holistic understanding of human behavior,
  • addressing both emotional needs (humanistic) and intellectual processes (cognitive).
  • [A] /
  • [CO2]

questions.question: Elaborate on the significance of Erickson's theory in understanding human behaviour. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate on the significance of Erickson's theory in understanding human
  • behaviour.
  • Erik Erikson’s Psychosocial Theory outlines eight stages of human development,
  • each with a specific psychosocial conflict that must be resolved.
  • Examples of stages:
  • • Adolescence (Identity vs. Role Confusion) – Critical for developing a stable
  • self-identity.
  • • Young Adulthood (Intimacy vs. Isolation) – Focuses on forming deep
  • relationships.
  • Significance:
  • • Explains how personality develops over the lifespan.
  • • Highlights the influence of social and cultural factors.
  • • Offers a framework for understanding challenges at different life stages.
  • • Helps in psychological counseling and educational support by addressing
  • developmental crises.
  • [An]/
  • [CO4]

questions.question: Explain the application of conformity, compliance, and obedience in understanding the behaviour of an individual. / [CO5] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the application of conformity, compliance, and obedience in understanding
  • the behaviour of an individual.
  • Conformity: Changing one’s behavior or beliefs to match group norms.
  • o Example: Dressing a certain way because your peers do.
  • o Shows how group influence shapes attitudes and actions.
  • Compliance: Responding favorably to a direct request.
  • o Example: Donating to a cause when asked, even if you didn’t plan to.
  • o Important in marketing, sales, and social interactions.
  • Obedience: Following orders from an authority figure.
  • o Example: Milgram’s experiment showed how people obey authority
  • even when it conflicts with personal conscience.
  • o Explains behavior in hierarchical settings (e.g., military, workplace).
  • These concepts help in understanding social influence, group dynamics, and the
  • mechanisms behind behavior modification in various contexts.
  • [A] /
  • [CO5]

questions.question: Analyze the impact of group behaviour on individual identity. / [CO5] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the impact of group behavior on individual identity.
  •  Group behavior strongly shapes individual beliefs, values, and attitudes.
  •  Individuals often conform due to social pressure (conformity).
  •  The theory of social identity was developed by Henri Tajfel.
  •  Group membership gives a sense of belonging and self-esteem.
  •  Peer groups significantly influence behavior, especially during adolescence.
  •  Can lead to positive outcomes like cooperation, teamwork, and social support.
  •  May also result in negative effects like peer pressure, groupthink, or loss of individuality.
  •  Individuals may change behavior to match group norms and expectations.
  •  Group identity can influence decision-making and moral judgments.
  •  Understanding group behavior helps social workers manage group dynamics and interventions
  • effectively.
  • [A] / [CO5]
